title: Starmer Pledges to Bring Britain 'Closer to the Heart of Europe' Despite Leadership Crisis
detail: On 18 May 2026, Prime Minister Keir Starmer — facing continued calls to resign from nearly 100 Labour MPs — used parliamentary and media appearances to double down on his government's legislative agenda, particularly its flagship commitment to closer EU alignment. Starmer pledged to make the UK-EU 'reset' — including dynamic regulatory alignment, a UK-EU youth mobility scheme, and reduction in post-Brexit veterinary checks — a defining feature of his premiership. The King's Speech (13 May 2026) had contained legislation enabling closer EU ties as part of its 37-bill programme. Critics from Reform UK and sections of the Conservative opposition condemned the pledge as a 'back-door Remain'; pro-European Labour MPs welcomed the ambition. Starmer explicitly cast the EU agenda as evidence of his government's direction, rebutting calls to step down by pointing to a coherent legislative programme.

media.caption: Starmer pledges to bring Britain closer to the EU despite the Labour leadership crisis
